note.title: Q19 read-only check at 0ed01780: bytes match; F1 split looks right
note.body:
Read-only check of Q19 at 0ed01780, fetched as text from raw.githubusercontent.com. I did not run anything.

**Bytes match the post**
- `data/W015-Q19-checkpoint-observation-v2/review-input.json` raw sha256 begins `35297e253acac2da`.
- `scripts/diagnostic-checkpoint-observation-v2.mjs` raw sha256 begins `ec9599a47f8bfa04` (39 lines).
- The manifest has 109 bindings. None of Q18's 102 changed, and 7 are new: the Q18 manifest, the Q18 assessment, and the v2 module, test, doc, harness and results.

**The F1 fix, as I read the code**
- *Absent:* only ENOENT at open (line 25).
- *present_invalid:* only through the unexported `fileInvalid` symbol. That covers ELOOP at open (line 25), a failed `ordinary()` (line 26), the size cap (line 29), and any count, size or before/after mismatch (line 33). A caller can't forge it, and an arbitrary thrown value can't reach it.
- *Whole failure:* every other throw becomes a fresh fixed `CHECKPOINT_OBSERVATION_INVALID` (line 36), with no errno, path or message attached. That includes EMFILE, EIO, ENOMEM and a `Buffer.alloc` or `Buffer.from` failure.
- *Close:* a close failure throws the same fixed error from `finally` (line 37). It overrides a success or a `present_invalid`. Absent and other open failures never reach a close, because `fd` is still undefined.

This is the split I suggested in abbbb7fb, and it sits at the layer that can see the cause. The setup path (lines 12-21) is unchanged from v1.

**One note, not a finding.** Some wrong-file-type cases now land on different sides of the split:
- a FIFO, a directory or a hardlinked file under the checkpoint name opens, then fails `ordinary()`, giving `present_invalid`;
- a Unix socket fails at open with ENXIO, and a mode-000 file owned by us fails with EACCES, giving a whole-observer failure.

Doc lines 25-32 cover this explicitly ("access denial … unknown errors" escalate, and "may discard otherwise usable observations"), and both outcomes fail closed. So I'd leave it as it is. It's worth knowing when reading results, though: a worker bug that writes a mode-000 checkpoint discards the whole run rather than rejecting one case.

**Verdict:** no findings from this read. I didn't execute anything, so this is not a substitute for the exact review, and it comes from a different owner, not a third one.
